additional_info.body:
Hello,
On November 30, a client tried to charge on the charger 170002732, site 47643, between 1
:47:36 PM and 2:00:42 PM CU TIME, but he could not charge because he first had a problem with the authorization and then, when he tried again, the charge started but the charger didn't deliver any power. He tried also on the charger 170002450 but again he had a problem with the POS, so the charge never started.
Can you please check the logs?
Thank you.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0464912-DC/Si-D/IT-[MP/R9 170002450] Check on logs CRM:03097000255
additional_info.body:
Good morning Rosita,
I am reaching out from the Technical Support Team in regards of ticket
ID0464912.
The ticket has been opened for charging issue and authorization on two chargers in San Martino Buon Albergo. I had a look at the logs reported at the timestamps reported, and these are my findings:
On charger MP/R9 170002732
:
A session is started on DC2 at 2025-11-30T12:46:54.
It is authorized via RFID, and the session successfully starts at 2025-11-30T12:47:18. The session ID is: 506121216
Energy is delivered, and the EV charged form 30% till 67%.
Session is stopped from EV side at 2025-11-30T13:05:47.
On charger MP/R9 170002450
I do not see any charging attempt at the timestamp mentioned.
If I understood correctly, the customer faced issues to pay with the POS.
Unfortunately, being the IM30 PAX terminal integrated in our Sicharge D as a Cloud Payment terminal, from Sicharge D side we do not have visibility at all of the Payment process and authorization.
The communication sequence: POS  --> Fortech --> NTT Data Backend --> Sicharge D (via OCPP). Therefore, from charger side, we only receive a RemoteStartTransaction when the authorization and payment process is successful and communicated from the Backend to the charger. We do not have visibility of any failed payment, as all this communication is limited between the POS and Fortech.
Hope my analysis provided you with an explanation. Please let me know if further support is required for this ticket, otherwise I will proceed to close the ticket.
Looking forward to hearing feedback form you soon!
With kind regards,

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0464912-DC/Si-D/IT-[MP/R9 170002450] Check on logs CRM:03097000255
additional_info.body:
Good morning Rosita,
Thank you for your reply. I apologize for the confusion, let me provide you with a clarification on the analysis I provided you:
The timestamps that you reported are CU time, so the actual time at the charger.
The chargers logs are reported in UTC time, so one hour before the time in Italy.
Based on this consideration, I checked anyway also the logs as if 13:47 was the UTC time. Here is a summary of my analysis:
On charger MP/R9 170002732
:
The analysis I reported in my previous email refers to 2025-11-30T12:46:54 UTC time, hence 13:47 in Italy.
As per my previous email, the charging started on DC2 at
2025-11-30T12:47:18. (13:47 Italy time), the session ID is: 506121216, and it was stopped at 2025-11-30T13:05:47 (14:05 Italy time).
No other charging attempts happened on this charger in the meanwhile.
No charging attempts attempts happened between 13:47 UTC time and 14:10 UTC time.
On charger MP/R9 170002450:
​​​​​​​
There is no log referring to an attempted charging or an attempted authorization on this charger from 12:00 UTC time (13 Italy time) until 14:30 UTC time (15:30 italy time).
As per my previous email, due to the nature of the architecture of communication between the POS, the payment provider, the OCPP Backend and the charger, from a charger point of view we can see an attempted charging session only if the plug is connected to an EV. From an authentication point of view, we can see only a RemoteStartTransaction, which means that the user authenticated and paid via POS. In case this authentication phase fails at POS side, or between POS and Fortech, or between Fortech and NTT Data Backend, from a charger point of view we do not see anything, because it is out of our control.
I hope I managed to provide you with a clear explanation of the logs for the events reported.
Please let me know if you have further questions or if further analysis is required. Looking forward to hearing feedback from you!
With kind regards,

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0464912-DC/Si-D/IT-[MP/R9 170002450] Check on logs CRM:03097000255
additional_info.body:
Good evening Rosita,
Thank you for your reply and for providing the correct timestamps for the analysis. Here is the outcome of my analysis:
On charger MP/R9 170002450:
Between 2025-11-30T14:38:14 and 2025-11-30T14:47:18, the EV with EVMAC
f0.7f.0c.2d.a4.1e
attempted to charge four times.
The first session failed at 2025-11-30T14:39:29 during P03_CableCheck phase. as the EV sent to the charger a SessionStopRequest.
For the last 3 sessions, the vehicle sent us a SessionStopRequest even during P01_Authentication phase, not even allowing the user to authenticate with the POS.
On charger
MP/R9 170002732:
​​​​​​​
There is a session starting on DC2 at 2025-11-30T14:39:40 by EV:
44.1d.b1.b0.dd.84
The session is stopped normally without fault by the EV itself at 2025-11-30T14:47:27
The EV
f0.7f.0c.2d.a4.1e
(the one mentioned for the other charger), authorizes via POS at 2025-11-30T14:58:40 and connects to DC2 at 2025-11-30T14:58:56
Also here, the EV sends a SessionStopRequest before CableCheck, asking to interrupt the session.
The EV disconnects and no further attempts appear.
​​​​​​​From my analysis, it is clear that the issue is Vehicle related, as the EV was suddenly interrupting the communication with the charger with no reason.
I hope I provided you with clarification to your logs analysis request. Please let me know if further actions are required from our side, otherwise I will proceed to close the feedback once your feedback is received.
With kind regards,
